v.

PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.

              REPLY OF OLD DOMINION ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE
     TO RESPONSES TO INITIAL BRIEFS OF PJM INTERCONNECTION, L.L.C. AND
                THE INDICATED PJM TRANSMISSION OWNERS

        Pursuant to the Order issued in the above-referenced proceeding on December 18, 2025,

and the Notice of Extension of Time issued on January 23, 2026, Old Dominion Electric

Cooperative (“ODEC”) submits this reply to certain of the responses to the Initial Brief and Joint

Responses of the PJM Transmission Owners to Paper Hearing Questions and the Initial Brief of

PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”).

        In its Reply Brief, ODEC expressed its general agreement with the proposals submitted by

PJM and the Indicated TOs. ODEC also expressed its willingness to adopt the Indicated TOs’

proposed rates for the new Firm Contract Demand and Non-Firm Contract Demand, subject to

clarification. ODEC explained its support for the Commission’s acceptance of both filings, subject

to further compliance filings as necessary to address the following issues described in its Reply

Brief: (1) clarification of PJM’s proposed requirement that an Eligible Customer must be


                                                2
 designated to take transmission service on behalf of a Co-Located Load and provide PJM with an

authorization from its Relevant Electric Retail Regulatory Authority (“RERRA”); (2) with respect

to the PJM TOs’ proposal for PJM to provide billing credits to reflect revenues associated with the

new Grid Reliance Charge as well as revenues for Non-Firm Contract Demand Service, the

individual TOs will need to either confirm that their formula or stated rates and metrics reporting

enable the direct crediting by PJM, or provide whatever revisions are necessary in order to do so;

(3) PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners will need to address how to charge regulation and

black start service to an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of Co-Located Load; and (4)

the Commission consider whether any protections are needed for local utilities or TOs should they

need to take the extraordinary measure of disconnecting an Eligible Customer taking service on

behalf of Co-Located Loads, if the Eligible Customer’s use of the transmission system exceeds

contract demand or are called upon for Load Shedding and Curtailment. In such instances, the

local utility or TO should not be liable for legal, financial or other damages that might be

experienced by an Eligible Customer.

          ODEC’s position on PJM and the Indicated TOs’ filings remains as stated in ODEC’s

Reply Brief. ODEC reiterates its request that the Commission address these issues, particularly

clarification regarding how a generation and transmission cooperative like ODEC will meet PJM’s

proposed requirement that an Eligible Customer must be designated to take transmission service

on behalf of a Co-Located Load and provide PJM with an authorization from its RERRA. 1 ODEC

submits this brief response to address two issues; the proposed measures to protect reliability, and

the proposed Grid Reliance Charge.




1
    ODEC Reply Brief at 6-7.

                                                 3
             A. PJM Must Ensure that Service to Co-Located Loads Does Not Adversely

                Impact Reliability

        ODEC continues to express its support for PJM’s proposal for escalating penalties in the

form of disqualification and pauses in service for failures to shed load or curtail, as well as for

failures in control technology, and/or protection system misoperation. 2 However, as ODEC

discussed in its Reply Brief, clarification is needed regarding how the Eligible Customer and

RERRA for Co-Located Loads will be applied to generation and transmission cooperatives like

ODEC.3 PJM’s implementation of its penalties must not subject ODEC or its member distribtion

cooperatives to service interruptions or disqualification, or financial penalties, as a result of

requiring ODEC to serve as the Eligible Customer. Instead, such penalties must be limited to and

borne by the Co-Located Loads.

        ODEC also continues to support development of financial penalties, while recognizing that

financial penalties alone will not be sufficient to preserve reliability. The need to ensure reliability

of the transmission system is paramount. To that end, ODEC disagrees with parties who have

suggested that financial penalties alone will suffice, and that PJM’s proposed remedial measures

are overly harsh.4 ODEC does not agree that PJM’s proposed suspension and disqualification

measures are unfairly imposed regardless of fault and will make the services unduly risky for many

loads.5 Reliability of the transmission system is critical and financial penalties imposed on the

Eligible Customer, alone, will neither preserve reliability nor protect other users of the

       ODEC also agrees with the Indicated PJM TOs that PJM should clarify that (1) each new

transmission service, including Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, will be conditioned

on the implementation of control technologies and protection systems that will ensure Co-Located

Loads do not exceed their specified level of transmission service; and (2) necessary control

technologies and protection systems may be required on both the customer’s side and the

Transmission Owner’s side of the point of interconnection. 6

           B. The Commission Should Accept the Indicated PJM TOs’ Grid Reliance

               Charge

       The Indicated PJM TOs proposed a Grid Reliance Charge to reflect the fact that Co-

Location Arrangements are physically connected to and synchronized to the transmission system 7

and use the transmission system.8 Although some have asserted there should be no charge at all

for customers that reserve zero to a de minimis amount of transmission service,9 the disagreement

among parties is not focused on whether there should be a Grid Reliance Charge, but instead on

how such charges should be determined. 10 ODEC continues to support the Indicated PJM TOs’

Grid Reliance Charge, in addition to charges for Black Start and Regulation Services. These

services may not reflect the full use or reliance on the transmission system by Co-Location

Arrangements, and Co-Located Loads must pay their fair share. While other proposals might be

 just and reasonable, the Indicated PJM TOs have adequately supported their proposed Grid

Reliance Charge and the Commission should accept it as filed.

       WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, ODEC requests that the Commission consider

this response as well as the requests in ODEC’s Reply Brief and accept PJM’s and the Indicated

PJM Transmission Owners’ proposals for transmission service to Co-Located Loads, subject

compliance filings as necessary to address the following: (1) clarification of PJM’s proposed

requirement that an Eligible Customer must be designated to take transmission service on behalf

of a Co-Located Load and provide PJM with an authorization from its RERRA; (2) with respect

to the PJM TOs’ proposal for PJM to provide billing credits to reflect revenues associated with the

new Grid Reliance Charge as well as revenues for Non-Firm Contract Demand Service, the

individual TOs will need to either confirm that their formula or stated rates and metrics reporting

enable the direct crediting by PJM, or provide whatever revisions are necessary in order to do so;

(3) PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners will need to address how to charge regulation and

black start service to an Eligible Customer taking service on behalf of Co-Located Load; and (4)

the Commission consider whether any protections are needed for local utilities or TOs should they

need to take the extraordinary measure of disconnecting an Eligible Customer taking service on

behalf of Co-Located Loads, if the Eligible Customer’s use of the transmission system exceeds

contract demand or are called upon for Load Shedding and Curtailment.
